## Overview

The Timeline \| Calendar feature offers a quick, convenient way to view and update date-related information in your TrackVia application. From activities to tasks, projects, and beyond, Timeline and Calendar views help visualize and manage your data.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635459867)

In this article, we’ll move step-by-step through the process of configuring and modifying

Timeline \| Calendar views.

**Before we get started, ensure that you have the following steps completed:**

**1.** Locate a table in your application containing records that you would like to visualize in a

Timeline \| Calendar.

**2.** Ensure that the table contains at least two [Date](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8811398834971 "Link: http://help.trackvia.com/knowledgebase/articles/323926-field-types"), or [Date/Time](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8811398834971 "Link: http://help.trackvia.com/knowledgebase/articles/323926-field-types"), fields. These should correspond to the “Start” and “End” dates of your activity, task, project, etc.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34834050496539)

## Navigation

To create a Timeline \| Calendar view you can either create a new view or navigate to an existing custom grid view in your application and click the View Options button in the top right corner (highlighted in red box below), and then click on "Timeline \| Calendar" in the drop down options.

![Selecting Calendar View Type.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34810727630235)

_**Note**: **You will not be able to convert a table's Default View into a Timeline \| Calendar view.**_

## Configuring Timeline \| Calendar Views

![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/MVJ_hWuE7QjBXZ-X2a6izMTto1-cnA-hUBTGtt_jC4KExwVY126eYlc7f-CIHZYyxWY8rAoMLq5HUIS6g_-lXelPT0cO5koJrxc9uw2YVko6iq3xsoEJQqz1NmSEOZn-Nkj8OSMB)

**Step 1: The Basics** Configure the Start & End Dates of your calendar records in the Timeline \| Calendar modal. In this example, the "Project Start Date" field and "Project End Date" field have been selected as the Start and End date of each calendar record:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34834671250459)

Configure how you would like the Timeline \| Calendar to load. You can set the default to display events starting with the current date/time, or load beginning at the earliest Start Date for a record on your table:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34834658050587)

Next, you see which filters were applied to your original grid view, quickly change the filter to another pre-existing filter, or navigate to [create a New Filter](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8720164750107) if you would like to see a new subset of the information included in your original grid view.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34834671255579)

_We'll leave this option blank in this example in order to see all of the records on our table._

**Step 2: Choose View Types**

Now that you’ve selected exactly what data should be contained in your view, you can customize the Timeline \| Calendar view itself.

![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/rCrazjRySUcD-lEEqOy41AmTUAx-meViOfdoiNZtVV9iBbC99SZboZG6kWOZqTWOgte4e20UlkIQbjPAE9LMDw9pG5YMtFAEnnu1hBbPWFhmLpAKPlXz13DxowQDnc4bSgzHSPKX)

There are currently three (3) View Types available for Timeline \| Calendar views: Timeline, Calendar, and Grid. Here, all three options are selected and the Default View Type is set to Calendar:

![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/qwkYjBAUMH3YnZrkgXuZcv3JRcSg9B-3OEKf295CQsuzU0NwCQonzK_Un_8koX4mCPJe9XPP-g8W3NiKaUGd77NhDEnBuj0iW44HHxy23Y5KsFiQ_Zk5WvQum28zD6UqXOPRcKsY)

Select up to three (3) fields to display on your Timeline \| Calendar records for easy visibility of record attributes without needing to click into individual records:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34834658057883)

Below is the final Calendar view with [conditional formatting](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8810091106075) applied to visually color code various Project Statuses.

The conditional formatting rules were set up as shown below:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635466395)

And the calendar displays the Project records with the conditional formatting colors as shown below:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635468699)

**Step 3: Timeline Configuration**

_**Note**: When you were selecting the View Types to toggle through on your Timeline \| Calendar view you may have been unable to select the **Timeline** checkbox. Hovering over the checkbox displays this message:_

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635473819)In order to utilize the Timeline View Type, TrackVia needs to know how to group your records in order to deliver the best possible display experience. To accommodate this, **your table is required to have at least one Parent table related to it**.

_**Note**: Unfamiliar with configuring Parent-Child relationships in TrackVia? Explore more [here](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8782624148379)._

If your table is the Child in at least one relationship, you’ll be able to select the Timeline View Type and proceed to Step 3. If you only need to view your records in a Calendar & Grid view, you can simply click “Save Settings” and skip to the **Features** section below.

With the Timeline View Type selected, you’ll have access to Step 3, where you can configure your Timeline view. Select the timeframe you'd like to apply to your Timeline view:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635479579)

_**Note**: All of the settings we’re configuring can be changed after the view is Saved._ Select the desired relationship to group by. Timelines are grouped by relationship fields included in the view. In this example, the records are grouped by the related parent record on the "Customer" table:

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635482907)

Set the Preferred Parent view for this grouping. This is particularly useful for identifying records on your current table that are not associated with a Parent Record in the given relationship.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635487259)

_For example, let’s say that you have Projects that you accidentally forgot to link to a Customer. When you select the \[ **Customer\] Default View** you will be able to quickly see these Projects, grouped by the fact that they have no related Parent record (remember: in this example, you are grouping by the Project’s related Customer). Then you’ll be able to quickly drag and drop the Projects on your Timeline to dynamically associate them with the proper Customer._

Finally, click “Save Settings” to see your new view.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34835635488923)

Within Timeline \| Calendar views themselves, you can easily drill into your data, adjust the Start & End dates associated with your records, or move an entire event. This will automatically change the related date fields on the record you are modifying.

![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/v4Rv-WgzRGtr1Dk954plCiwznQfrkpJbT8OCuN2iSN4ZqfYuyiVGLCz3qvmxMrbTc0-Qw1K1C_6Mjcsaj8KHFz7EoUSei-5SAWmz9JWdAexjf8lHovSFcBwpGZ52-KBA8YloL-lo)

As mentioned above, you can easily use the Timeline View to change the Parent record your current data is associated with. For example, here we can see that there is an activity, “Timeline \| Calendar Training”, which is not associated with any location. You can easily drag the calendar card into a different row or timeslot to update the record:

![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/Ap3kPpU-xWFI8pmCq3iajXX0ips7brG-1yhRuoV4ov1lsK1sI633NRJjNXtwcMb7W6iYIWU5Rm-q-iyLkt1eOfBXfrqzXm3TQdT55-2B9XglvgBivSyeS1ZRS_I2ruIBuC95SxVy)

_**Note**: All Timeline \| Calendar views will display the first 1,000 records. If you need other records to display, we suggest applying a filter to the view._

## FAQs

**Q:** How do I see exactly when an event Starts or Ends during my day?

**A:** Use [Date/Time](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8811398834971) fields instead of basic Date fields as the Start & End Dates when configuring your Timeline \| Calendar in order to see exactly when events are scheduled to Start or End.

**Q:** What happens if the End Date on one of my records is accidentally set to occur before the Start Date?

**A:** When viewing a record with an End Date occurring prior to the Start Date, where the Start and End Dates are simple Date fields, the event will not appear in the Timeline view.

_Follow up_: When viewing a record with an End Date occurring prior to a Start Date, where the Start and End Dates are Date/Time fields, the event will not appear in the Timeline view.

**Q:** Is there any restriction to the type of fields I can put on my Timeline \| Calendar record labels?

**A:** No. Location fields will display the Location’s Latitude & Longitude coordinates. Image and Document fields will display the name of the attached image or document if one is present on the record.

**Q:** What happens if one of the Date fields I’m using on my view is accidentally deleted?

**A:** In this case, you’ll be prompted with an error message when attempting to load the view indicating that you need to reach out to one of your app admins.

**Q:** Can I put Timeline \| Calendar views on my Dashboards?

**A:** Yes, like any other view, Timeline \| Calendars make great additions to your Dashboards.

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8810091106075-How-to-use-conditional-formatting#main-content)

# Overview

Conditional Formatting is a powerful TrackVia feature that allows users to easily change the text and background colors of their records. Quickly identify records that meet any specified business criteria with only a few clicks.

A few popular use-cases for Conditional Formatting involve:

- Being able to see records color-coded by Status.
- Quickly being able to identify currency fields above or below a specified threshold.
- Easily call out overdue, or soon-to-be-due, items.

Conditional formatting can be applied to standard grid views, Timeline \| Calendar views, and Maps.

# Navigation

To set up Conditional Formatting, navigate to the Toggle View Options dropdown on any custom View and select “Conditional Formatting”.

![How_to_use_conditional_formatting_1.jpg](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11078552367259)

Once launched, click “+ Add Rule” to configure the first rule to apply to this View.

> ![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/nPhEUW3lwSm67NAHigG2QvCYR9UosgVrsWYLxZieMniOFQPLSBZSUfBYeW37x936iC5fVbeHa4R4ZwwZXi3vIr53Nr3B7ktLTjOk7KDQS3cBlFYaJz5lmZmE6650UzljVtrWO_eY)

> 1\. Users are able to highlight an entire row of data, or just a specific field within the View. When highlighting, change the color of the text that will be displayed, the background, or both.

> ![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/VkrQeOmVC1_aDUznxpFJF5kJNEykvWxxSHFrEVHXJgUdHhwFWBKsvLOpJ0t6xKVKqS2nObCnnZrYALMILl923qFOJAMfRBTKBzJUl92JehH2IaiAxz_NtnyyscvvGOd3swbvcvfJ)

> 2\. After applying a color scheme to the Rule, set the Conditions for when the rule should be applied to your View.

> ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/F16LLq2ECfiiKifiLzJNHPUrmF-2b8vsl-VaohlbvjMeKK-aRgkYBQACjvwC2m8f1TpsRN5brU6pAbVGqR6n4WcN7mG5dmFFitSXGi8PkkUjzhbihrkLhkIGYdDohCWIMPW1fgV8)

> ![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/0XHZ2L9reu8D2Wm4wYmZWFXsv1Fdo-1JaslVJAJ262oW4PQiwLc4Fak2C4liGsIx7zXUo2aP54U4nkM4ckza5muCULdvW_bHviuh08_CwLrHaGo6cVfjlzfOs-dYYbsJ8q2OutKm)

> 3\. Click “Apply” and then “Save your rule, or add another to your view.

_**Note:**_ You can add multiple Rules to your View. Rules are applied in order, which can affect how the formatting is applied. For example, Rules will be applied in numeric order; Rule #1, followed by Rule #2, etc.

> ![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/JdlaaoxyZS7q0172Ej8yKztgWJyGUfB1oFfPDBCrD-DufGBDqzeOL8kAc-T1tcqdHp1gWN_JM8SR-EHSBbxXQcHvCjIhBFkdAvLZzexhsdLBNQp06h6bPqTn0a8wgzco7PzBuP2t)

> 4\. If the Conditional Formatting on a view only applies when certain criteria are met, note that it will be applied your grids in embedded child views and dashboards.

> ![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/HF0iMRbMcl2oXjKAJ8zkBiaa63UdaFWzE34zwOuze3Ql5oS7KGxPJhfh-xWtb66iXxfHRT_ziXVc4r-8uCs8QJqp10HRDKDQbKCoYzN71y_V6aLVi7RUOC08j282SKyCXAJKgHuk)

Once Conditional Formatting has been applied to a View, note that it will remain even if the View is Converted to a [Timeline/Calendar](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8810292092059) view or [Map](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8780565442587):

## Conditional Formatting on a Calendar

![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/xc571-M49Z84-JLnDOwdpW7oswMGklydYX_g7TN3DamA4EjhNvw64vVUMeHbyKWy8WI5C50nVNcdtz57FQwhJXDiyHb3K0QZzzm2Yz0x_T_wXXyScLCqRMNOS-yuLkrxM5uKzJ3p)

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8721004049947-How-to-use-form-show-hide-rules#main-content)

Would you like to make your TrackVia data entry forms more user friendly by only displaying fields when they are needed?  The “Show/Hide” feature allows you to break up large, complex forms and workflows, showing your users only what they need to see, when they need to see it.

After adding a field on the edit form page, hover over the field and click the pencil icon to edit that field's settings.

![edit a field on a form.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/25808992354203)

Next, select the Show/Hide tab and choose the 'When this Condition is True' radio button to create a rule to determine when that field should appear.  Building a rule is similar to how the criteria for a filter is built.  You can use AND and OR logic to create conditional groups, if needed.

![show hide conditions.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/25809009096859)![](http://trackvia.uservoice.com/assets/99982881/Screen%20Shot%202016-04-13%20at%203.41.09%20PM.png)

In this example, the Repair Comments field will only be shown when a Repair Status is selected and someone is Assigned To the audit.

“Show/Hide” also works on mobile - just like other TrackVia features, what is built on the web seamlessly translates to the mobile application.

In another scenario, let’s assume you have a vacation request workflow you’re building, with a simple approval step.  If for some reason the vacation request is not approved, you want the approver to give a reason why the request was denied.

_Image 1: Vacation Approval Form does not show "Reason" field unless the "Manager Approval" field has the option "No" selected_

![Vacation Request Approval Form reason field hidden.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/25808992368667)![](http://trackvia.uservoice.com/assets/100028043/Screen%20Shot%202016-04-14%20at%208.42.35%20AM.png)

_Image 2: If the "Manager Approval" field has the option "No" selected, then the "Reason" field is shown on the form_

![reason field shown with Manager Approval as No.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/25808992378267)

With “Show/Hide”, we’ve made it incredibly easy to set your form up so the ‘Reason’ field only shows when you choose ‘no’ for your approval.  Doing this allows you to clean up your forms considerably, making them easier to use and faster to fill out.

**\*Please note that a Multi-Select Widget is not considered a field, so the widget will not display as an option for Show/Hide criteria. Furthermore, values will only save for sections that are showing at the time a record is saved. Data in hidden sections or fields will be discarded.**

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8810602836507-How-to-use-the-Lanes-view#main-content)

TrackVia's Lanes views (commonly referred to as _Swimlanes_) help you create an agile workflow that is simple to manage for everyone. Lanes are useful for visualizing a business process that involves more than one department, or has many stages and/or steps to go through in order to be completed.

Lanes Views consist of categories represented by vertical columns called _**Lanes**_ (highlighted in red below), and the records in the view appear as _**Cards**_ (example of a Card highlighted in green box below) that can be moved from one lane to another either by dragging and dropping the card from lane to lane, or editing the record and changing the value of the in the Drop Down or Relationship field that is used as the categories for the Lanes.

### ![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34846954391707)

## Converting a View into a Lanes View

**Note that to create a Lanes view a Drop Down field or a Relationship field linking to a Parent table must be included in the view**. You can either create a new custom view or choose an existing view that includes at least one of those field types, and then open the view menu and select Lanes.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34847012535195)

### _Note: Lanes views will only include the first 250 records from the grid view that is converted into the Lanes view._

## Set up your Lanes

In the "Name" field you have the option to edit the name of your Lanes view.

Next, choose the Drop Down or Relationship field that you wish to organize into lanes (see red box below), choose which values from the Drop Down or Relationship field to be displayed as the Lanes (see purple box below), and choose up to three (3) fields to be displayed on the Cards (see green box below).

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34847012536731)

Note that you can check the "Allow custom sort within each Lane" checkbox (see red box below) to enable a custom vertical sort for each Lane.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34846954396443)

This will allow you to not only drag & drop cards from one lane to another, but to move the cards to a specific spot _within_ a lane and save it in that spot.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/34846954397979)

After customizing your settings, click "Save", and you've created your Lanes View!

While interacting with the Lanes view, moving a card from one lane to another will update the record associated with that card's Drop Down field to the corresponding Drop Down option for the Lane the card is placed in. For example, in the GIF shown above, moving the card from the "In Progress" lane to the "Complete" lane will update that record's Task Status Drop Down field value to "Complete".

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8663584412571-How-to-use-your-mobile-device-offline#main-content)

The TrackVia mobile app can be used in an offline mode. With the offline feature enabled, you can create records, edit their drafts, and upload when you are connected. Furthermore, by turning on automatic sync, the application will upload data when it detects an internet connection.

### Enable an Offline Offload Table

An offline offload table is a single table, that contains the following fields:

- Single Line Field named "APP"
- Single Line Field named "FORM"
- Application User Field named "USER"
- Document Field names "FILE"

This table can be housed in a separate application, or it can be added to an existing application, although there can only be one offline offload table for the account. It is important to enable "Create" permissions to any users utilizing the application in offline mode.

_**An account admin must contact TrackVia Support to complete configuration of the Offline Offload table for the account, prior to mobile offline use. See the [Contact TrackVia Support](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/16575804153115) article.**_

Once everything is set up, the end result for a failure that is offloaded will be a record on the Offline Offload table, it will have the App that the user was working in, the Form, who the user is, and a zip file with the changes. An account admin will then be able to resource the zip file of the changes, and implement them in the account online.

### Enable Offline Mode

Offline mode is enabled in a user's Role setting. To do so, simply edit the role, and select the table under Assign Views and Forms. When assigning a form for creating new records, check the box to "Create records offline" and save the changes.

![UV97.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11110368908955)

Once the feature is enabled, the next step is to sync your mobile device with your TrackVia application. From your mobile device, open the TrackVia mobile application. Next, click into your settings and select 'Sync Now'.

![UV98.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11110371183387)

![UV99.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11110373392283)

The sync button will cache any forms and views which have been enabled for offline support on your local device. This allows you to add new records or edit existing ones from views that are offline-enabled when there is not an available internet connection.

Jake Marwilcommented  · November 4, 2014 12:52 PM ·

Hello,

It sounds like you may have added a Document type field to your table. These fields allow you to attach a file or document into the record – for example, a Word document, .pdf file, spreadsheet or video clip.

If you go to add a record to your table and click on the Document field, a window will pop up allowing you to find the file you would like to upload. Once you select a file and click to save your record, the document will be uploaded directly into TrackVia. Once uploaded, it will appear as a link that allows the user to open or save it. There is a file size restriction of 40 MB.

Please let us know if you have any further questions.

Regards,

Jake

Andrewcommented  · December 1, 2014 4:41 PM ·

Esrana,

I am not sure why this may be occurring without seeing the specifics of your account. A thought is that it may be happening because there is an issue with the order of operations in the calculations.

I would suggest adding a set of parenthesis around the entire calculated currency formula of "Margin" to ensure that the Margin value is calculating correctly before being passed to "Mark Up". If you would like additional support, please submit a ticket by using the "Help" button in the top right of your screen, and I can provide more specific help by looking in-depth at your formulas.

Alexcommented  · November 26, 2014 10:47 AM ·

Hi Esrana,

Since currencies are numeric fields in the table, the calculated percentage should still output correctly: {Currency A} \ {Currency B} = %.

There may be another issue with the formula or the fields being divided for the percentage to work properly. **Justin Mauldincommented****· June 30, 2017 12:24 PM**

Hi Michael,

Thank you for reaching out to us with your question.

When importing data into a Location Field on your table, you have to have one field on your file that has the longitude and latitude coordinates separated by a comma in it to get a successful import and mapping of the point into the field.

If you are trying to import the actual address in your file, you will need to convert your address to longitude and latitude coordinates (outside of the TrackVia system) and then attempt your import again.

Below, is a link to an article we have in our knowledge base that helps walk you through the needed setup for a successful import, as well as, some other details about Location fields.

[https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8780565442587-How-to-plot-a-record-on-a-map](https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8780565442587-How-to-plot-a-record-on-a-map)

Thanks again,

Justin

Below, is a link to an article we have in our knowledge base that helps walk you through the needed setup for a successful import, as well as, some other details about Location fields.

[https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8780565442587-How-to-plot-a-record-on-a-map](https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8780565442587-How-to-plot-a-record-on-a-map)

Thanks again,

Justin

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/16372851849755-Importing-FAQ#main-content)

**What types of files can I import?**

There are two types of files that can be imported into TrackVia: .xlsx and .csv. It’s also possible to copy and paste data into the import wizard, as long as it’s in a comma or tab separated format. If you need more flexibility on how you import data into the system, check out one of our [integration options](https://developer.trackvia.com/).

**How long is the import going to take?**

This is dependent on many factors and is difficult to predict. For the most part, imports complete rather quickly (within a couple minutes). However, it’s possible that importing can take much longer, based on the following factors:

- Number of records in the file
- Number of columns in the file
- App scripts that will run when a record is added or updated
- Number of triggered fields that will run when a record is added or updated

**How will I know when the import is finished?**

If you stay on the import screen while the import is running, you will be notified in the application that it has completed. If you leave the import screen while the import is running, then you will receive an email when the import has completed. The email will contain the error report, if there were any errors.

**Who can import data?**

Only admin users can import data into tables.

**I need to update the records in a table via import but the record ID is not unique. What should I do?**

The best way to handle this scenario is to temporarily adjust the record ID of the table to something more unique. An auto counter field is a good option. After the import finishes, you can change the record ID back to the original setting.

**How do I stop an import that is currently running?**

If you need to stop an import that is currently running, please contact the TrackVia Support team for assistance.

**How many imports can I have running at once?**

There can only be one import running in your account at a time. This is a safeguard that we have in place to ensure your data integrity and application performance.

**Is there a max number of rows or columns that can be imported at once?**

There is no maximum number of rows or columns that can be imported into a table, as long as the file size is under the maximum limit (40 MB).

**Is there a limit to the size of the import file?**

The import file cannot be larger than 40 MB. If your file is larger, try breaking it up into smaller files and running multiple imports.

## What's New

Lanes views, also known as Swimlane Views, have been given a fresh look and additional functionality! We've added more flexibility in building lanes/columns, sorting your cards and choosing what is shown on each card.

- Parent values can be used as lanes! Now you can use a relationship field to to create your lanes. For example, if you have States as a related Parent table to your Projects table, you can now select States to build a Lanes view.

- A custom vertical sort can be enabled and saved for that view. This will allow you to drag & drop a card to a specific spot _within_ a lane and save it in that spot. This works great when you need to prioritize your cards within a Lane!

- You can select any Drop Down or relationship fields you have in your view to display as Lanes.

- Additional fields can be added to a card (up to 3). This is great to see more information at a glance when viewing your cards.


![Screen_Shot_2019-01-14_at_3.05.45_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11118162790683)

### The Details

To start, you must create a custom view.  If your view contains a Drop Down field and/or a Relationship (Link to Parent) field, you will see the Lanes option in the hamburger menu of the new view.

Click the Lanes option to open the Lanes Setup window.  You may edit the View name here.

To use a Drop Down field:

![Screen_Shot_2019-01-14_at_2.42.03_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11118205315611)

1. Choose the Drop Down field. In the above example, we have chosen Project Stage.

2. Choose the Drop Down values you want to use as lanes.  The order you choose will be the order in which the lanes are displayed.  One hundred (100) is the maximum number of lanes.

3. (Optional) Choose the display fields for each card.  The Record ID will always be used. You may choose up to 3 more fields.(\*)  The order you choose will be the order of the fields displayed.

4. (Optional) Choose a filter or create a new filter.

5. (Optional) Check the box to allow custom vertical sorting within the lane.

6. Click Save Settings.


To use a Relationship (Link to Parent) field:

![Screen_Shot_2019-01-14_at_2.48.37_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11118235463835)

1. Choose the Relationship field. In the example above, we have chosen State as the Relationship field. State is a table connected to Projects.

2. Choose a Preferred Parent View.  Best Practice is to create and choose a Custom View (i.e. not Default even though that is what we are showing above).

3. Choose the Parent values you want to use as lanes.  The order you choose will be the order in which the lanes are displayed.  One hundred (100) is the maximum number of lanes. In the example above, we have choose California and Alabama as the Parent values

4. (Optional) Choose the display fields for each card.  The Parent Record ID will always be shown. You may choose up to 3 more fields.(\*)  The order you choose will be the order of the fields displayed.

5. (Optional) Choose a filter or create a new filter.

6. (Optional) Check the box to allow vertical sorting.

7. Click Save Settings.


(\*) Display Fields

- All field types are available to display on a card except Image, Document and Checkboxes.

- Location fields will be the text values for Lat and Long.

- URL and Email fields will display as text (not clickable).


### What's Different

In the View Options (hamburger) menu for a Default view:

- "Lanes" no longer appears.


In the View Options (hamburger) menu for a Lanes view:

- "Create New View" has been removed.

- "Edit This View" takes the user to the general View Builder instead of the Lanes Setup modal.

- Use "Lanes" to create and edit a Lanes view.


Sharing a Lanes View

- All email shares will show a grid view of up to 250 records.

  - An ad hoc (immediate) share will show only the records for the chosen columns of the view.

  - Scheduled shares will show records for all the columns regardless of which were chosen to display.

### Notes

- Existing Lanes views will display as expected.  Choose the Lanes option to edit.

- Permissions are not violated.

  - Users with edit permission will still be able to drag a card from one lane to another.

  - Users without edit permission will not be able to drag a card vertically to re-sort a lane even if the Admin has enabled the option.

- Mobile functionality

  - iOS will continue to render a grid for all Lanes views.

  - Android will continue to render a Lane view when it is created with a Drop Down field.


    - As before, all columns will display.

    - As before, each card will contain the Record ID and 1 display field only.


  - Android will render a grid view for a Lane view created with a Parent relationship.

## Bugs Fixed with this Release

- Some users were having trouble saving changes to Quick Filters when many tabs of the same browser window were open. This is now fixed.
- A limited user without permission to delete records was seeing an "X" (delete icon) in a Lanes view.  The "X" to delete no longer displays for that user.
- Changes to a Lanes view which contained a relationship (Link to Parent) field were causing errors and not saving.  With the Lanes Enhancement release, users can edit Lanes views that contain relationship fields.
- Some fields were not displaying custom formatting in the Audit History of a record when the record was viewed from a custom form.  This is fixed.

# Improved User Management

Welcome to easier user management!  We’re adding a number of enhancements to help you find and manage your users more effectively.  Specifically, you can now Search, Filter and Sort your list of users. Further, additional ‘standard’ table controls such as Import, Export, Print & History are now available to you via the Options menu.  Last, but not least, we’ve added a new column of data to show the last time that your users logged in.

Note: User Groups were displayed on the grid view but is no longer.  You can drill into a user record to view the groups associated with that user.  Try it out today!

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.39.19_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116472269851)

# Search

Search is now enabled by default for the view.  Search will execute on the User ID, First Name, Last Name, Email, Time Zone, and Status. For example, I searched for "joh" and the below results were returned.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.40.20_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116510175515)

# Filter

You can now filter your list of users just like you can in other views.  You can filter on any of the fields in the Account Users table. AND & OR operators are available as well as conditions and condition groups.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.41.03_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116487929115)

# Sort

You can now Sort your users using the familiar sort functionality. You can sort on any of the fields in the Account Users table. The search order applies as it does in other views.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.41.41_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116569235739)

# Manage User Groups

The Manage User Groups button has been moved from a button at the top of the screen to an item in the Options menu to better align with our user experience.  The functionality of managing user groups has not changed.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.42.11_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116778385435)

# Add a User

Adding a user now happens in several places. First, the standard “Add Record” button has been added to the upper right corner of the view, to the left of the Options menu.  Selecting this button will take you to the Profile Information form where you can add a user. Second, you can now Import a CSV or XLSx with user information by selecting “Import” in the Options menu.  Last, when you are viewing a profile, you can “Save and Add New” records. The old “Add User” button & email field at the top of the screen has been removed.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.42.35_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116783891611)

# Import

We’re pleased to announce bulk import to your user table!  Adding users is now even easier than before. Simply select the options menu and then “Import” to start our import wizard.   Email is the only required field for import. When users are imported, they are set to “Unverified” and a verification email is sent to the user.  We will email you the import results when the import completes.

\*Note: You can only Import to Add today.  Import to Update is not available at this time.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.43.51_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116827459483)

# Export

Exporting works like it does on any other table.  Simply select the Options menu, then “Export” and a CSV will be made available to download with all data in the table.

# Print

Printing the table view works like it does on any other view.  Simply select the Options menu and then “Print” to get your printing options.

![Screen_Shot_2018-09-21_at_1.44.28_PM.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11116877514523)

# History

Audit history on Account Users is now available.  Select the Options menu and then “History” to view record changes or additions to this view.

![UV175.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11122586699803)

A highly-requested feature has entered the product here at TrackVia: App Admin access to Sandboxes! For developers and Super Admins who have been using [our Sandbox feature](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8727320719515) to prototype and manage changes to production applications, allowing App Admins to review and modify Sandboxes has been a long-standing request. We’re excited to deliver on this capability, so let's take a look at how it works:

**App Admin Experience**

If your account has Sandboxes enabled, App Admins will now be able to navigate to the new “Sandbox Environments” option in their Account dropdown in the upper right-hand of TrackVia:

![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/AgvDLdu35VEmAOOSjOlwP6onwbLgpUeHTLI8KZaaKwjEfAB6_UPrdd581MZlczgqLs2lt0FdDDjfwohoSCkLRg5kLWt5U8BklIvKK78SOL-WYG8TLyh0lw5UUQn9rTkJXtHZlKz4)

As expected, App Admins will see a list of all Sandboxes available to launch.

_**Note**: App Admins do **not** have the ability to create new sandboxes or delete sandboxes, only launch them for testing and development._

![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/wrB62sX08S-da7tF-wEI6po0KSgXMvuA9p9Th0VxXGfudxpfKR82DVzSx84cfhPW228TPhH3TfjB6dQVFh6es_QAapEfHK9GbcBo3h7r7Wv7fePplCZNl5yqri7WmQHYQJKXQn6R)

When selecting the Sandbox to launch, the App Admin will see a list of Applications to log into within that Sandbox (this list reflects those Apps where they are an App Admin in your production account). After selecting the app the App Admin will choose which Role they would like to assume within the Sandbox (from the full list of Limited User and App Admin Roles available).

In addition to allowing App Admins to assist with development in Sandboxes and review development made by Super Admins, this feature is also a great way to impersonate a Limited User role to understand exactly what your end users are seeing!

**Updates to Super Admin Experience**

While the Super Admin process for accessing Sandboxes remains functionally the same, we made some visual changes to the modal that displays when the Super Admin chooses a user:

![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/P5Fo8EY5-i78Jf2zOeuAiIxUNrXn4lCY9I21SXS_nqgAqHvx4fA1WCFkVfCwEr-fZuS00UkDQ5Q2R6HTzF_J-XR3ApI5pUiBwBqI6A-FHy059T5mUaln-tMAVuBN9KS1xtFrLuIO)

# Backup and Restore

Accidents happen. Sometimes you can undo whatever mistake you’ve made, other times you need to go for more drastic measures. This feature, Backup and Restore, is for those times.

There are two parts of Backup and Restore as the name suggests; Backup and Restore. We’ll talk through each separately.

This feature is only available for Super admins.

## Backup

When you execute a Backup of your account, you are doing so to your entire account. All users, apps and data across your entire account will be backed up.

Backups are discreet, you and your team will be able to use TrackVia as the backup occurs. However, it is a snapshot of the system as is, so for example if you’re doing an import when you run a backup, the backup will only contain information in the system at the time of the backup, so you’ll likely not get all of your imported data (if the import process continues after the backup starts)

### What is not backed up:

Files (documents, voice memos, signatures), Images, Microservices

- These items are stored externally, so when you delete them from TrackVia, they are deleted from the external system and not recoverable from a restore.

Sandboxes

- Sandboxes will maintain their current state regardless of backup or restore.

**How to access Backup and Restore**

To access Backup and Restore, navigate to “My Account”

![UV67.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054046702363)

Where you’ll find Backup and Restore at the end of the “My Account” menu.

![UV68.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054051103899)

Clicking on Backup & Restore, you’ll be brought to this page:

![UV69.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054054357019)

The Backup and Restore page shows you all manual backups that have occurred within the last 7 days.

At this time, the list does not include the backups automatically created every night at midnight. To restore from one of these backups, please contact support. Eventually, these automated backups will appear in this list, but not in this first release.

The second tab on the Backup and Restore page is the Activity Log. The Activity Log will show you what activities have happened, ordered chronologically. For example, when you perform a restore of your account, the system will actually back up your account before doing the restore, just in case you need to back out of the restore to the moments just before.

![UV70.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054092288923)

Which then brings us to…

## Restore

A “Restore” of your account is something you will likely do in only the most dire of circumstances. When you perform a restore on your account, you are rolling the entire account back to the time when the backup was performed.

### A couple of caveats about this procedure

- This process will take your account offline for the entirety of the process. When the process starts, people who are in the system will be signed out and shown the “Maintenance Mode” page. This includes mobile users.
- We do not have specifics on how long your account will be in maintenance mode. It will depend on the size of your account and how busy the system is at the time of the restore. It could be several hours.
- Files, images and microservices are not included in backups, do not restore your account to try to get deleted files back. Restores only include apps and data.
- If you’ve added a user after the restore point, you will need to re-add that user.

### Restore failures

There are certain cases when you will temporarily not be able to restore your account. In these instances, the person requesting the restore will try to restore and immediately be presented with an error message, “We’re sorry, we can’t restore that backup right now. Please try again later!”.

These cases are:

1. A sandbox is being created.
2. An import is in progress.
3. A backup or restore process is already running for the same account.
4. The maximum number of backups (for all accounts) are happening at this time.

When a restore fails an email will go out to the user who attempted the restore.

### What does a restore process look like?

From the Backup and Restore page, you will click on the ‘restore’ link.

![UV71.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054125396379)

After clicking this link, you’ll see a modal to read and confirm.

![UV72.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054150246171)

And your account will go into maintenance mode.

![UV73.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054153745563)

As well as your mobile clients

![UV74.jpeg](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054190518043)

Here’s what the process looks like:

![UV75.gif](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11054223425563)

Additional information is available in our knowledge base [here](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8727295515035).

# What's New

We're so excited to bring you a brand new way of analysing the data you have in TrackVia: Pivot Views!

A Pivot View is a versatile tool to help you summarize the information in a table by slicing and dicing data so you can look at it from different perspectives. It works by grouping records together based on several factors, then summarizing the data from those records, either by counting the number of records per group, or by using a specific summary function (like sum, average, or maximum) on another field. It's useful when you have lots of numbers that need summarizing, when you want to compare subsets of data, or when you’re trying to find trends in your data.

Our new functionality comes out of the gate with pivoting on multiple rows / columns, sorting pivot data, applying conditional formatting, and an easy to use designer.  We think you'll love it, give it a try today!

![UV146.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121686266651)

## How it works

Pivots are created by converting an existing **grid** view (default or custom) into a Pivot view.  Simply hit the Options menu in the upper right and select **Pivot** from the menu.  Our new Pivot designer slides out from the right and you can apply your desired settings:

![UV147.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121689291931)

Name your Pivot something unique, select some Rows, Columns and Values and Save your settings.  Your new Pivot is displayed!

![UV148.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121739146395)In the above example, I selected my Rows to be 'Inventory Items', my columns to be the 'Create' date, rolled up by Quarter and the Sum of the 'Cost Subtotal' as my summary function.

To apply conditional formatting, hit the Options menu again and add a Conditional Formatting Rule.  I created a Pivot rule where the Cost Subtotal is less than $100.

![UV149.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121742242715)

Check out our [knowledge base article](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8810005198875) to find out more details on how to configure your pivot, things you can do with it (export!) and more.

Coming soon to our GOV, HiPAA and Private environment customers.

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/8186381756571-Introducing-TrackVia-Integrations#main-content)

This is a big step for us - yes, we’ve had “integrations” in the general sense through our APIs, our Microservice architecture and even Zapier for a while, but this is different. TrackVia Integrations is a premium feature that we've added to the TrackVia platform, it is the result of a partnership we've forged with Workato, the leading integrations platform for enterprises. (If you're interested in seeing what TrackVia Integrations has to offer, please reach out to your account manager)

The reason for this partnership is simple - as we’ve continued to try to solve the various integration challenges you have run into, we discovered a few core elements that we wanted to address.

1. We wanted an integration solution that would connect easily with Enterprise systems. SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, Zendesk, etc.
2. We wanted an integration solution that could handle advanced logic (like when to add and when to update).
3. We wanted something that was just as easy as TrackVia.

So we finally did it. Here’s what you can expect from TrackVia integrations and how it all works.

TrackVia Integrations, like TrackVia itself, is a platform for building integrations between systems. Each integration has a few different parts:

1. Connectors. These are the systems you’ll trade data between.
2. Recipe. This is a unique set of instructions that will take data from one connector and pass it to another.

But let’s first get into TrackVia Integrations. To start, once the feature has been turned on in your account, you’ll access from your account menu.

![UV155.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121968581019)

And just in case you’re actually looking for the ‘old’ integrations page (now called Microservices) we’ll drop you off on a page that will explain the difference between the two and take you to the right place.

![UV156.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11121977123355)

Note that when you enter TrackVia Integrations, you’re in a new tab in your browser, and the interface looks a little different.

![UV157.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11122061851291)

To get started, just click on the “Create a new recipe” button, and TrackVia Integrations will walk you through the process of making your first recipe! To get back to TrackVia, you can either close the tab in your browser or choose 'Logout' from the account menu (upper right).

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/9436600933019-IsBlank-function-not-working-for-Parent-fields#main-content)

Running into an issue using the isBlank function on a parent linked field. The field is blank (Verified using the quick filters on the view), but the formula returns the result as if the field had data. This is the same issue that is described in this post: "Invisible Characters in Link-To-Parent Fields??".

Example: if(isBlank({Field Name}),"Blank","Not Blank") will return "Not Blank" even through the field appears to be blank.

Jon shared this idea · Feb 9, 2022

Hi Richard,

While we currently do not have the ability to copy an entire application, you do have the ability to rename an application. You can do so by clicking the Admin button on the top left of the screen and then clicking on the Table Relationships button. In the top left corner of the Table Relationships page is an edit button next to the application name. Please let us know if you have any further questions.

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/9436527951771-Is-it-possible-to-sum-the-contents-of-a-parent-table-with-the-contents-of-the-child-table#main-content)

I've been building a working project application using a number of parent and child tables.

Some of the parent views carry rate card values for specific services and these are displayed within the child view when selected. There are ad hoc services in the child table with free currency fields for varying prices.

Is it possible to create a calculated field to sum the total the free currency fields, with the rate card parent fields to autogenerate a total order value per project?

I've tried to use some excel formulas sumproduct & sumif but these are not supported - any advice would be appreciated.

Michael Leneghan shared this idea · Jul 14, 2022

**Alexcommented  · June 10, 2015 2:55 PM**

Hi Justin,

While there is not a definite limit to the number of if() statements that can be nested, there is a limit to the size of the query that is generated by the formula. Briefly scanning over the attached formula, there is one function that is not supported by TrackVia: IFERROR. This function would need to be removed or modified in order for the table to save.

Additionally, the formula as a whole looks to be too large and would hit the query limit. We recommend submitting a ticket through your account to support so that we may better understand what the purpose of the formula would be. This would also allow us to better understand the use case and provide specific recommendations for a scalable solution.

Regards,

Alex

**Alexcommented  · June 10, 2015 2:55 PM**

Hi Justin,

While there is not a definite limit to the number of if() statements that can be nested, there is a limit to the size of the query that is generated by the formula. Briefly scanning over the attached formula, there is one function that is not supported by TrackVia: IFERROR. This function would need to be removed or modified in order for the table to save.

Additionally, the formula as a whole looks to be too large and would hit the query limit. We recommend submitting a ticket through your account to support so that we may better understand what the purpose of the formula would be. This would also allow us to better understand the use case and provide specific recommendations for a scalable solution.

Regards,

Alex

[Skip to main content](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/9437454789659-Is-there-a-toggle-for-case-sensitive?sort_by=votes#main-content)

I know that the search function is not case-sensitive, but uploading records to the database seems to be. We use email address as a unique identifier when uploading new info and will always end up with duplicate records when someone enters their email address differently than previous. For example, [Ta305@gmail.com](mailto:Ta305@gmail.com) versus [ta305@gmail.com](mailto:ta305@gmail.com) would create a dupe.

Is there a toggle somewhere to tell the DB to ignore upper case?

Anonymous shared this idea · Apr 19, 2018

## Related articles

- [Triggered Fields vs. Calculated Fields](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/related/click?data=BAh7CjobZGVzdGluYXRpb25fYXJ0aWNsZV9pZGwrCBtH4sv8BzoYcmVmZXJyZXJfYXJ0aWNsZV9pZGwrCBvsI1SVCDoLbG9jYWxlSSIKZW4tdXMGOgZFVDoIdXJsSSJLL2hjL2VuLXVzL2FydGljbGVzLzg3ODIzMzM3NTcyMTEtVHJpZ2dlcmVkLUZpZWxkcy12cy1DYWxjdWxhdGVkLUZpZWxkcwY7CFQ6CXJhbmtpBg%3D%3D--a600e675f6c6497b52acb6ac6b0a18ffa0fcb2ea)

- ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/180499253c8b18ed34c847a538106e12?default=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.zendesk.com%2Fhc%2Fassets%2Fdefault_avatar.png&r=g)



[Tiffanie Staver](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/profiles/7920567741467-Tiffanie-Staver)

- 2 years ago

**TrackVia(Community Manager, TrackVia) commented  · April 19, 2018 5:08 PM**

To confirm here, you are correct in your findings. Import to Updates require an exact case-sensitive match to the Record ID of the record you are mapping your update to. This cannot be changed at this time, however there is a quick workaround that may be helpful in this scenario. The goal is convert your email addresses to be completely uppercase in both TrackVia and your import file to ensure that they always match. First, you would need to added a triggered or calculated text field to your table with the following formula:

upper({Your Email Field})

This formula will convert all of your email addresses to uppercase. You can then set this new field as your Record ID so that it is used for your import mappings.

From here you just need to get the email addresses in your import file to be uppercase as well. I believe this can be achieved a few ways in Excel, but the quicker way I have found is to use the UPPER text function, which looks like this:

=UPPER(your fields)

Now that your TrackVia table and your import file both contain strictly uppercase values you should avoid any case sensitivity issues.

I hope this is helpful. If you have any further questions regarding this solution or if we can field any further questions, please let us know.

**Derrick Kotluscommented  · June 9, 2015 4:49 PM**

Hi Jill!

It sounds like you are adding child records (notes) to a parent record (meetings). The only way to add multiple records at a time would be through an import with an excel spreadsheet. Alternatively, you could use the "save and add new" button on the form to quickly jump to another blank form. If we are misunderstanding your question, please contact TrackVia support at [support@trackvia.com](mailto:support@trackvia.com) with additional details so we can take a closer look for you.

Hope this helps!

Derrick

Alexcommented  · October 30, 2014 1:04 PM ·

Hello,

This is a great enhancement suggestion that is on our radar for our product team. Currently, finding duplicates is not a native feature in TrackVia yet. We will be sure to pass along this request to our development team and will keep you informed as this enhancement progresses.

It sounds like the goal in this case is to avoid creating duplicates. To do this, you'll want to select the Update and Add option when importing the excel file. This option will queue TrackVia to match the existing records in TrackVia to the records in the excel file, update the matches to reflect the data in excel, and any excel record that doesn't have a TrackVia match will be created as a new record.

Regards,

Alex

- 2 years ago

Andrewcommented  · March 11, 2015 5:14 PM ·

Hello,

An alternative method, while not as sophisticated as our Classic platform feature, would be to use the Summary View (Grouped By view) to sort, and then count to find duplicate entries. Steps to use this method are as follows:

1) You can create a new field that concatenates different values that you want to find duplicates on. For example, you can create a calculated text field that pulls together the name of the individual and the email - the concatenation is completed with an ampersand in the middle: e.g., {Name} & {Email} So, we would be searching for duplicates where both the Name and Email match.

2) Now, a new view can be created - to group and count values with this new field. This is called a Summary View. Create a new view on the table, and on the Format tab, select this new calculated field in both dropdown boxes: (Apply a calculation and Group your results) and ensure that the calculation to be performed is "Count"

3) The output will be a collapsed grid and click on the second column to sort by the Count. Now, any entry greater than 1 means that there is a duplicate record for the criteria that was used in the new field.

4) Each record will have to be deleted manually, perhaps by opening the record in a new tab and selecting Delete

Please contact us if you have any additional questions!

Thanks,

Andrew

Hello,

This is a great enhancement suggestion that is on our radar for our product team. Currently, finding duplicates is not a native feature in TrackVia yet. We will be sure to pass along this request to our development team and will keep you informed as this enhancement progresses.

It sounds like the goal in this case is to avoid creating duplicates. To do this, you'll want to select the Update and Add option when importing the excel file. This option will queue TrackVia to match the existing records in TrackVia to the records in the excel file, update the matches to reflect the data in excel, and any excel record that doesn't have a TrackVia match will be created as a new record.

Regards,

Alex

Andrewcommented  · March 11, 2015 5:14 PM ·

Hello,

An alternative method, while not as sophisticated as our Classic platform feature, would be to use the Summary View (Grouped By view) to sort, and then count to find duplicate entries. Steps to use this method are as follows:

1) You can create a new field that concatenates different values that you want to find duplicates on. For example, you can create a calculated text field that pulls together the name of the individual and the email - the concatenation is completed with an ampersand in the middle: e.g., {Name} & {Email} So, we would be searching for duplicates where both the Name and Email match.

2) Now, a new view can be created - to group and count values with this new field. This is called a Summary View. Create a new view on the table, and on the Format tab, select this new calculated field in both dropdown boxes: (Apply a calculation and Group your results) and ensure that the calculation to be performed is "Count"

3) The output will be a collapsed grid and click on the second column to sort by the Count. Now, any entry greater than 1 means that there is a duplicate record for the criteria that was used in the new field.

4) Each record will have to be deleted manually, perhaps by opening the record in a new tab and selecting Delete

Please contact us if you have any additional questions!

Thanks,

Andrew

Hello Linda,

**Alexcommented  · October 31, 2016 8:27 AM**

Hi Rod,

This can be done using a TrackVia user field on your tables. This field allows you to pick your agents name from the list of users in your account then filter on this field. The filter can detect the current logged in user based on the user field for each record.

For example, you would create one view with one filter based on the current logged in user for the user field and all users will see different results based on the records where their respective name appears in the user field. More information on this can be found in our Knowledge Base: [https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8720164750107-How-to-create-a-filter](https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8720164750107-How-to-create-a-filter)

Let us know if you have any questions!

Alex

**Alexcommented  · October 31, 2016 8:27 AM**

Hi Rod,

This can be done using a TrackVia user field on your tables. This field allows you to pick your agents name from the list of users in your account then filter on this field. The filter can detect the current logged in user based on the user field for each record.

For example, you would create one view with one filter based on the current logged in user for the user field and all users will see different results based on the records where their respective name appears in the user field. More information on this can be found in our Knowledge Base: [https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8720164750107-How-to-create-a-filter](https://trackviasupport.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8720164750107-How-to-create-a-filter)

Let us know if you have any questions!

Alex

Is there a way to set up a master dashboard which everyone logs into and they just see the files they are working on without having to replicate the whole setup for each user?

Mariyacommented  · March 11, 2020 5:46 PM ·

Hi Glen,

Thank you for reaching out! If you are referring to the 'Location at Creation' feature that allows Admins to require location and capture it automatically, the location would only be captured at record creation, and the value would stay the same with record updates. If your goal is solely to capture location when a record is updated for the first time, you could remove the Location field from the form used for record creation, and only have the Location field on the form for record editing purposes. Once a user updates the record using this form, the system would automatically capture their current location. However, unlike the 'Location at Creation' feature, there is not a way to require this field to be filled out if location services are disabled on a user's device, and the user has the ability to alter this location manually.

That being said, being able to capture location at record update and remove the option for users to enter a custom value would be extremely helpful, and this is an excellent suggestion for an enhancement! I have logged a ticket with our Product team for them to review and consider implementing this functionality in a future project. Once this feature is released to the system, you will be notified via email.

Let me know if I can be of further assistance in the meantime,

Thank you,

Mariya

Mariyacommented  · March 11, 2020 5:46 PM ·

Hi Glen,

Thank you for reaching out! If you are referring to the 'Location at Creation' feature that allows Admins to require location and capture it automatically, the location would only be captured at record creation, and the value would stay the same with record updates. If your goal is solely to capture location when a record is updated for the first time, you could remove the Location field from the form used for record creation, and only have the Location field on the form for record editing purposes. Once a user updates the record using this form, the system would automatically capture their current location. However, unlike the 'Location at Creation' feature, there is not a way to require this field to be filled out if location services are disabled on a user's device, and the user has the ability to alter this location manually.

That being said, being able to capture location at record update and remove the option for users to enter a custom value would be extremely helpful, and this is an excellent suggestion for an enhancement! I have logged a ticket with our Product team for them to review and consider implementing this functionality in a future project. Once this feature is released to the system, you will be notified via email.

Let me know if I can be of further assistance in the meantime,

Thank you,

Mariya

Hi Esrana,

It sounds like we want to take the values from one table and make them into a drop down in another, related table. If this is the case, this is done through the creation of the relationship field. This will present as a drop down field in the child table that allows you to determine to which parent record to relate the child record.

## Role/User management

![UV10.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052301387803)

You can now add users in bulk, and even easily move people who were previously assigned to other roles.

## Dashboards

![UV11.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052362161563)

When you add a Dashboard to the role, the system will automatically add all of the resources on the Dashboard to the role for you.

## Flows

![UV12.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052368399131)

Likewise with Flows, when you add a Flow to your role, all of the resources included in the Flow will automatically be added to the role.

## Resources

![UV13.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052421747227)

We’ve added a new Forms section that gives you finer control over forms. With this capability you can now have multiple create forms on a table.

![UV14.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052453979419)

We’ve also made the system smarter to alert you when you might be missing necessary permissions on a form. For example, if you add a preferred parent view or a child view to a form, TrackVia will make sure you know to add that resource or permission to the role.

![UV15.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052457749275)

We hope you find the roles page much easier to use - and if you have any suggestions, please share!

## What’s Fixed?

- We resolved an intermittent permissions error that was being thrown incorrectly when interacting with relationship fields while adding new child records to a table.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/22278342621339)

- We resolved an intermittent error that was being thrown incorrectly when attempting to add new child records.

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/22278342625947)

- We resolved an issue for users interacting with TrackVia in a mobile web browser, as opposed to the native app, that was preventing them from interacting with relationship fields.
- We resolved an issue that was preventing users from being able to scroll easily within dropdown and relationship fields when adding child records to a table.
- We resolved an issue that was leading to some Views, in particular Lanes Views, intermittently “blanking-out” or turning into a white screen.
- We resolved an issue that was causing Grouped Views to not display an individual records within the groupings.
- We fixed an issue causing intermittent permission errors when a relationship field is utilized as a filter source for multiple Dependent Dropdowns.
- We fixed an issue with relationship fields being used in Dependent Dropdowns that was leading to the filtered relationships not being cleared when the filter source field was changed.
- We fixed an issue with the browser tab name not populating correctly on Dashboards

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/22278342628763)

- We fixed an issue leading to many rows in the Roles and Permissions builder unnecessarily being highlighted yellow after making a change to a role.
- We fixed an issue intermittently leading to Gantt charts “blanking-out” or presenting a white screen with no way to navigate to the View editor.
- We fixed an error when selecting the custom colors for a Gantt chart, leading to the error “None is not a valid Hex color”.
- We fixed an issue with Quick Filters appearing to have no conditions set, while records are still filtered.

API 23.39

## What’s New

- Comments in Formulas! We’re happy to announce that you can now add in-line comments to formulas you write in Calculated and Triggered fields. When writing a formula, simply use the following syntax for single line comments or multi-line comments.

  - Use double slash “//” for single line comments

  - Use slash asterisk for multi-line comments “/\* \*/” don’t forget to close your comment with the asterisk slash!

![UV45.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11053482044315)

## What’s Fixed

- Fixed a bug where a scheduled share did not honor the view sort

- Fixed a bug where a quick-filtered view ad-hoc share would not honor the filter

- Fixed a bug with in-cell edit validation for date/date-time, email, currency and number fields

- Fixed a bug where you could not create a flow with an Edit step directly after an Add step

- Fixed a bug where share links would not take the user to their record if they were not logged in

- Resolved an column name readability issue on Pivot views when using a parent field as a column

- Enhanced our forms so that long file names in a document or image field wrap appropriately

- Added back the ability to double click on a field in the view filter builder and have that field be automatically added to the filter.

- Fixed a bug where in some cases on tables/views, navigating between fields using the 'tab' button, changed / selected the first available value in Relationship and Drop-Down List fields inadvertently.

- We’ve unified the usage of “Default” across the product to make it more clear when you are interacting with a default view, default form etc.

- Fixed a UI issue where in some cases on the Form Builder, adding a Child View, the icons for grids and graphs changed when dragging them around.

- In some instances when changing a form field from read-only to having a default value, the value was not always populating. This has been fixed.

- Fixed an issue when editing checkboxes on a form, users may accidentally check the field.

- Fixed an issue where when a user has a favorite app and is then removed from that app, they always end up on an error screen. Now, the user will be redirected to their next app.

# What's New?

In an effort to continue making access to TrackVia resources as easy as possible for mobile users, we have added additional support for 'deep links' and 'universal links' when utilizing the iOS app, enabling end users to get directly to their work in the installed mobile app from links shared via email, text, chat, or any other method delivered on mobile.

_**What's a 'deep link'?**_

A deep link is a specific type of link formatted to direct a user to a specific location within a mobile app installed on their device, rather than the generic dashboard landing page or sign-in page.

_**Differences from normal, 'universal link' URLs**_

Deep link URLs are formatted differently than regular URLs. For example, while a link to a Form to add a new record might look like [https://go.trackvia.com/#/apps/1/tables/8/records/new/form/9](https://go.trackvia.com/#/apps/1/tables/8/records/new/form/9) in your browser, a properly formatted deep link would be: com.trackvia://apps/1/tables/8/records/new/form/9

With this release, all forms of deep and universal links should open directly in the installed app when attempting to direct users to a specific:

- View
- Form
- Record
- Flow

# What's Fixed?

- If a user was in the process of entering data on a Form and backgrounded the App before saving the record, and then accessed a link to a different part of TrackVia, unsaved Form data was previously being lost. We corrected this to ensure that the appropriate "Save data" / "Leave Current Flow" modals are always presented to allow end-users to Save in-flight data before proceeding to a different part of the application.
- Users operating in a TrackVia Trial account now have the ability to request that their Trial account be closed from directly within the Settings in the iOS mobile application.

iOS v6.7.0

Have you ever created the perfect selection of cross-table fields for a Map, Calendar\|Timeline, Lanes, or Pivot view and then wanted to re-use that same data for another view?  Well, now you can.

## Introducing Revert a View to a Grid

**Map, Calendar\|Timeline, Lane, and Pivot Views now support two options to change or reuse the view type.**

### Revert to a Grid

- Selecting "Revert to Grid" will **change** the current view type to a grid view.
- The selected filter, conditional formatting, and role assignments associated with the original view type are retained.

For example, from a Map view

![UV23.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052822330523)

### Copy to New View

- Selecting "Copy to New View" will **create a copy** of the fields to use in a new grid view.
- The selected filter and conditional formatting of the original view type are retained.
- Role assignments associated with the new Grid View are not retained.

The new grid view will need to be added to desired roles.

For example, from a Pivot view

![UV24.png](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/11052825806235)

# What's New?

In an effort to continue making access to TrackVia resources as easy as possible on mobile, this release is the first of a series of releases to update our support for 'deep links' when utilizing the Android app, setting the stage for universal links and new types of notifications.

_**What's a \`deep link\`?**_

A deep link is a specific type of link formatted to direct a user to a specific location within a mobile app installed on their device, rather than the generic dashboard landing page or sign-in page.

_**Differences from normal URLs**_

Deep link URLs are formatted differently than regular URLs. For example, while a link to a Form to add a new record might look like _**https://go.trackvia.com/#/apps/1/tables/8/records/new/form/9**_ in your browser, a properly formatted deep link would be: **_com.trackvia://apps/1/tables/8/records/new/form/9_**

In a future release we will be adding additional support for regularly formatted links to quickly get users into the app. For now, any instances, integrations, or use-cases where you're leveraging deep links will work as expected, per the fixes below:

# What's Fixed?

- Previously, if a user was filling out a Form or working in a Flow, toggled away from TrackVia, and then clicked a deep link (from an email or other app) to take them back to TrackVia, their in-progress work was not saved. We have fixed this and users will always be presented with the appropriate "Save" or "Exit Workflow?" modal.
- If a user does not have access to a resource but clicks on a deep link attempting to take them there, they will be presented with the appropriate 'Insufficient Permissions' error, instead of simply being presented with an app spinner.
- Previously, if a user clicked on a deep link while the TrackVia app was closed, they would simply be taken to the login screen of the app. Now deep links to will allow the user to get to the target Form, Record, View, or Flow as expected.
- Previously, if a deep link did not specify the exact Form to open, links to specific records would not open as expected. Now, the app will open the appropriate Form based on the View ID specified in the link.
- We resolved an issue with Flows not initiating as expected in some scenarios where a user had newly installed the app and not yet accessed any Views.

Android v4.8.0

# What's New?

## TrackVia App Insights

TrackVia App Insights is a powerful new set of account management features now accessible on all accounts. Currently available to Super Admin, the first version of App Insights allows you to easily see, manage, and maintain all Application Scripts, Notifications, and Scheduled Shares configured in your account from one convenient, centralized location.  [Check out the full breakdown of App Insights and additional features that are in development here!](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/en-us/articles/26532183163675-TrackVia-App-Insights)

![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/26532174424859)

_Quickly access account resources from one central location, accessible under the App Overview dropdown of the Admin toolbar._

## Radio button display on web

Dropdown fields can now be rendered as Radio Buttons for easier data entry on Web! This setting is enabled on the Form Field settings for Dropdown Fields and does not impact the current behavior for rendering radio buttons on iOS and Android.

**![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/26533405286299)![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/26533405314075)**

_Note that users will always see a "None" option for dropdowns rendered as radio buttons to ensure that they can clear out the value from the field if necessary._

## Signature field input on web

Additionally, Image fields can now be configured to accept signature input on web! Similar to activating Radio Buttons, configuring Signature options is available in the Form Field settings.

**_Please Note that configuring an Image field to 'Display as signature field' will now cause it to render as signature input on both web and mobile._**

**![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/26533405344539)![](https://help.trackvia.com/hc/article_attachments/26533405360795)**

# What's Fixed?

- We fixed an issue with History data not displaying properly in on Records in some scenarios where bad data had been added to the record via OpenAPI.
- We fixed a minor UI issue affecting Record ID columns not greying-out appropriately after saving records in a Child View
- We fixed an issue with values populated in a Multiselect widget being cleared out if being added to a Form that is left open and unsaved for more than 2 minutes.
- We added additional handling to make sure that complex appscripts are able to execute without impacting customer experience of application performance.

API v.23.43

To limit access to a specific field on a form, you will need to create a new form that omits the fields you do not want the user to see. You will then need to create a new role and assign the user and the newly created form to the role.

We understand this method is not the most efficient, and we are looking for better ways to accomplish this. Please look for improvements to come and let us know if you have any further questions.
